title: More than Ukraine: How the Abu Dhabi talks laid bare Russia’s priorities – European Council on Foreign Relations
gist: Policy alert: the November 10-11, 2026 US-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi produced only a prisoner-exchange deal in principle, while Russia refused any ceasefire, demanded all of Donetsk and pushed a 'new Yalta' revision of European security. Barbashin argues Ukraine is Russia's entry point to a broader bargain, and Europeans must insist on indivisible security, resist bilateral non-aggression offers and refuse to trade an architecture redesign for Ukrainian peace.

insights.claim: Two days of US-mediated Ukraine-Russia talks in Abu Dhabi on November 10th-11th 2026 produced an agreement in principle on a prisoner exchange but no breakthrough on ending the war.
insights.speaker: Anton Barbashin
insights.so_what: No ceasefire in sight; don't price a near-term end to the war or sanctions relief.

insights.claim: Russia again refused any ceasefire or pause in combat until a comprehensive deal is reached, and chief negotiator Vladimir Medinsky reaffirmed Moscow's demand for the entire Donetsk region, which Ukraine rejected.
insights.speaker: Anton Barbashin
insights.so_what: Maximalist territorial demands keep the conflict active; supportive of continued European defence spending.

insights.claim: American envoys did not put forward new ideas that visibly shifted either side, and it is unclear which security-discussion elements they will carry to Moscow and Kyiv; in this vacuum Russia's framing risks becoming the default agenda.
insights.speaker: Anton Barbashin
insights.so_what: US mediation is not delivering; risk of a deal shaped by Russian framing over European interests.
insights.quote: Russia’s framing, which links any Ukrainian settlement to a renegotiation of European security, risks becoming the default agenda
insights.locator: Finally, US mediation adds further uncertainty

themes.theme: Russia's real aim: revising European security

insights.claim: Russia does not want a deal on Ukraine alone; it wants to revise the last 35 years of European security, treating Ukraine as the way into a much larger bargain.
insights.speaker: Anton Barbashin
insights.so_what: Any settlement would carry NATO-posture implications for central/eastern Europe, not just Ukraine.
insights.quote: Russia does not want a deal on Ukraine alone—it wants to revise the last 35 years of European security

insights.claim: Medinsky described the post-Yalta/Potsdam system as 'sick', with Ukraine merely the place where 'the abscess burst', and called for a 'new Yalta' implying Russian dominance of the post-Soviet space.
insights.speaker: Anton Barbashin
insights.so_what: Signals sphere-of-influence ambitions that threaten eastern flank states' security.
insights.quote: Medinsky described the post-Yalta/Potsdam system as “sick”, with Ukraine merely the place where “the abscess burst”

insights.claim: Russia's position at the talks revives the core of its December 2021 demands: a legally binding halt to NATO enlargement and possible reductions in NATO's military presence in central and eastern Europe.
insights.speaker: Anton Barbashin
insights.so_what: Watch whether US accepts NATO-posture concessions; would be a major shock for Baltic/Polish security.
insights.locator: Russia’s position at the talks revives

insights.claim: EU Commission, European Council, key-capital and NATO officials were present in Abu Dhabi but stayed outside the main negotiating room, and Russian representatives said they saw little reason to meet Europeans absent concrete European proposals.
insights.speaker: Anton Barbashin
insights.so_what: Europe lacks a seat at the table; decisions affecting European security may be made without it.
insights.locator: The format of the talks also marginalised

insights.claim: Russia's suggestion of bilateral non-aggression pacts with individual NATO or EU states is a classic divide-and-rule tactic, consistent with Putin's preference for dealing with Europe as a collection of capitals.
insights.speaker: Anton Barbashin
insights.so_what: Watch for individual capitals breaking ranks; would weaken EU sanctions and defence cohesion.
insights.quote: This is a classic divide-and-rule tactic

insights.claim: Europeans should insist that decisions on European security are indivisible, coordinate any responses to bilateral Russian overtures through the EU and NATO, and require a genuine ceasefire, withdrawal from occupied territory and verifiable offensive-capability limits before any security-architecture dialogue.
insights.speaker: Anton Barbashin
insights.so_what: Defines Europe's red lines; a breach would indicate weakening cohesion.
insights.quote: Europeans should not accept an abstract redesign of the security architecture as the price of peace in Ukraine.
